When `mirror.adr = true`, accepting a decision writes two artifacts from one
capture: the entry at `.dira/entries/dec-NNNN.md`, and a conventional ADR at
`docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md` following the host repo's existing convention (kazi's is
`docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md`, currently 83 numbered).

The direction of authority is strictly one-way:

- The **entry** is the record. It is what `dira why`, `dira map`, and `dira check`
  read, and the only thing that is queryable.
- The **ADR** is exhaust — generated, human-readable, expected by convention, and
  safe to delete. Deleting every ADR must lose no information.
- Edits to an ADR are **not** read back. If someone edits an ADR by hand, dira
  regenerates over it and says so. The fix is to edit the entry.

This is the honest resolution of the original complaint. The ADRs were never the
problem; not reading them was, and that is unfixable at the ADR layer because files
are pull-based. So the files keep existing for the humans and audits that want them,
and the retrieval path moves entirely to push — `dira brief` at session start,
`dira why` on demand. Nobody has to open either file for the system to work.

One number worth remembering as the test of this decision: kazi has 83 ADRs and the
person who wrote them does not re-read them. If dira ever requires reading a file to
function, it has reproduced that outcome with more machinery.
